purpose: One bounded necessary-condition relaxation of the Latin-preserving IPA pilot: remove every Latin identity anchor, without changing source, alignment, periods or alphabet family.
source_description: Frozen Cambridge US strings from the preceding pilot, stress marks, spaces and syllable dots removed; length marks retained. No fresh source lookup or alternative pronunciation selection.
alignment_warning: These are stipulated unchanged transformed-glyph positions, conditional on the prior pilot alignment. They are not a proved 97-character phonetic transcription. Phoneme counts are 10 and 9, raw glyph lengths 13 and 11.
equation: C_i = f(P_i) + k_(zero_based_i mod p) mod 26; equivalently f(P_i) - q_(zero_based_i mod p) = C_i with q = -k.
glyph_values: Every one of the 14 observed glyphs has an unknown value in Z/26Z. Values are shared and injective across glyphs; ordinary IPA Latin letters have no Latin-value anchors.
key: An unrestricted periodic sequence in Z/26Z; no keyword or language scoring.
canonicalization: One key-phase convention. Plus/minus key and phase changes do not add structures. True Beaufort is equivalent by negating the completely free glyph map. Global simultaneous f/q shifts are a 26-fold gauge, fixed by f(i)=0 when counting. This is not a Latin identity anchor.
analysis: Construct the exact weighted bipartite graph over glyph and phase nodes for the first window, and separately for both windows.
Solve each connected component with modular potentials. A nonzero cycle residual is an exact rejection certificate.
Reject distinct glyphs with equal potentials within a component. Otherwise each component has one free additive gauge; require disjoint shifted glyph-value sets across components.
Retain every solution as compact exact graph potentials and gauge-disjointness constraints, or exact counts if feasible. Never pick an appealing assignment as evidence.
For Berlin checks, distinguish first-stage forced outputs, gauge-dependent outputs and outputs requiring newly introduced glyph values. New glyph assignments are never predictions.
Stop after the 24 structures: no extra periods, transpositions, dialects, source variants or language optimization. A fit is compatibility, not evidence of the hypothesis or a complete decryption.
validation: One reproducible synthetic positive control per canonical structure, using all 14 symbols, an injective random glyph map and unrestricted random key, then verifying the generating assignment and graph solution.
Independent exhaustive tiny-ring checks comparing graph/gauge counts and feasibility with direct enumeration of injective glyph maps and all keys.
Machine-check every reported cycle or within-component collision certificate against the original equations.
scope_limit: The complete IPA vocabulary has more than 26 symbols. This only tests a necessary-condition relaxation on the 14 glyphs occurring in these two windows; it is not a universal IPA codec.
counting_limit: Use exact symbolic graph records whenever full first-stage enumeration is too large. If a bounded counter stops, label the count unknown and preserve the exact constraints; do not claim completed enumeration.
